lesson.title: Solving Linear Equations
intro: To solve a linear equation, isolate the variable by undoing operations while keeping the equation balanced.
When fractions are present, multiplying both sides by a common denominator can simplify the work.
When variables appear with parameters like \(a\), solve the same way by factoring the variable when needed.
Always check which answer choice matches the simplified result.

questions.explanation: Subtract \(2\), multiply by \(3\), divide by \(4\), and solve: \(x=14\).

questions.prompt: The solution to the equation \(\frac{2(3x-1)}{3}=x+2\) is
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by \(3\): \(2(3x-1)=3x+6\). Then solve to get \(x=\frac{8}{3}\).

When solved for \(x\) in terms of \(a\), the solution to the equation \(3x-7=ax+5\) is
questions.explanation: Move the variable terms together: \(3x-ax=12\). Factor: \(x(3-a)=12\). Then \(x=\frac{12}{3-a}\).

questions.prompt: When the equation \(6-ax=ax-2\) is solved for \(x\) in terms of \(a\), and \(a\neq0\), the result is
questions.explanation: Add \(ax\) to both sides and add \(2\): \(8=2ax\). Divide by \(2a\): \(x=\frac{4}{a}\).
